Do not draw a single trend line for revenue/EBITDA/capex across the FY2016/FY2017 boundary.

FY2015.basis: standalone, pre-demerger entity -- not comparable to later years

FY2016.basis: standalone, first post-demerger FY -- revenue jump vs FY15 is the demerger, not organic growth

FY2017.basis: standalone (no consolidated table available for this FY)

consolidated_alt.basis: consolidated -- first year available, materially the same picture as standalone.

FY2020.note: Sharp jump in depreciation, interest, borrowings and capex -- large debt-funded capex/lease-accounting (Ind AS 116) shift, and leverage build-up well before COVID hit in Q4.

FY2021.note: COVID collapse; last full FY with complete financials before insolvency proceedings began (2022).

beta: not sourced -- not located for FY2017/FY2019-era Future Retail; the name was delisted/extinguished in 2022-24 and third-party stat providers generally do not retain a usable historical beta for it.
forensic_flags_visible_as_of_scoring_dat: As of 2017-03-31: leverage already building (Borrowings Rs 1,079cr vs Total Assets Rs 6,938cr, ~16% of assets debt-funded, up from a near-zero base at demerger) and EBITDA margin thin (3.4%) for a company growing revenue >2x/year post-demerger -- a diligent analyst could flag 'aggressive expansion funded by debt with thin margins' at this date, but nothing yet resembling fraud or imminent distress; this reads as an ordinary aggressive-growth-retailer risk profile, not yet a blow-up signal.

As of 2019-03-31: Borrowings had grown to Rs 2,657cr (2.5x FY17 level) while EBITDA margin only inched up to ~5%, and Debtor/Inventory days stayed low and stable -- the balance-sheet leverage trend is the clearest PIT-visible warning at this date; nothing in the FY19 numbers themselves yet shows the COVID-driven collapse (that hits FY20-21, all post-dating this scoring date).

The real blow-up driver (COVID-19 store closures 2020-21 compounding an already leveraged balance sheet, followed by the Amazon dispute and NCLT insolvency 2022) was NOT visible in FY2017 or FY2019 fundamentals -- this is closer to 'aggressive-growth-retailer-meets-tail-risk-macro-shock' than a slow-motion accounting fraud like PC Jeweller or CG Power, which matters for how this name-date's usability/DCF result should be interpreted.
